headline: Improving growth outlook

highlights: The lower end of the guidance requires a CQGR of 2.6% over the next two quarters – achievable, in our view.
EBIT margin remains at ~14.8% for H1FY27 (near lower end of guidance of 14.75–15.75%), as the company continues to invest for growth.
Management expects DSO to improve with OCF/PAT at 80% for FY27 (vs. 51% normalised for H1FY27).
In-line revenue led by BFSI, TMT and Insurance Revenue (CC) grew 3.3% QoQ/9.7% YoY, in line with our and consensus estimates.
valuation: Mphasis Tria: Traction beginning to scale Mphasis Tria's early traction began to scale in Q2, with the first deployments going live across multiple clients and verticals.

Tria is a proof point in large-deal evaluations and is opening business budgets, such as lending origination, payment exception processing and client onboarding in BFS, AI-led operations transformation at large insurers and on-demand intelligence for technology clients, which has significantly increased the addressable market.

The company has retained its target of 80% OCF/net income for FY27 and expects historical conversion levels in FY28, as none of the USD 900mn+ of H1 TCV required material cash investment and short-cycle deals rise.
watch: Insurance returned to growth (+1.8%), supported by Tria-led optimisation in underwriting, claims and risk.
Others declined 6.4% as build-work moved to run, while the healthcare sub-segment within Others grew on the back of recent wins, including a large deal, and is expected to become a key growth driver.
